findings.heading: ## **base** R
findings.proposition: The Vietnamese opening sentence splices an untranslated English clause into the middle of the Vietnamese sentence: 'Cac lenh trong **base** R functions to conduct statistical tests. co the duoc su dung de thuc hien cac kiem dinh thong ke.', so the topic sentence is stated twice and the Vietnamese sentence is broken by a full stop that the English original does not have.
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader opening the base R section meets a sentence that does not parse and an English fragment ending in a full stop, so the section's introduction reads as a copy-paste error rather than as the statement that base R functions can run these tests.

findings.heading: ### T-tests (gtsummary)
findings.proposition: English says the t-test compares the difference in means for a CONTINUOUS variable in two groups; the translation says 'su khac biet ve trung binh cua mot bien trung binh' (the difference in mean of a MEAN variable), which names a variable type that does not exist.
findings.reader_consequence: The Vietnamese reader is never told that add_p(... ~ 't.test') applies to a continuous variable, and may try it on a categorical or already-summarised column.

findings.heading: ## Correlations
findings.proposition: English identifies **corrr** as a package (in the tidyverse family); the translation says 'su dung lenh **corrr** tu package **tidyverse**' (use the corrr COMMAND from the tidyverse PACKAGE), making corrr a function belonging to tidyverse and repeating this in the next sentence ('Lenh nay cung cho phep...').
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader who loads only tidyverse will look for a corrr() function, not find it, and will not know that corrr is a separate package that must be installed and loaded (it is loaded via p_load in the setup chunk).

findings.heading: # Simple statistical tests
findings.proposition: English says the page showcases the common tests and links to FURTHER DOCUMENTATION (external package documentation and Wikipedia); the translation says it links to 'cac phan khac trong cuon so tay nay' (other sections in this handbook).
findings.reader_consequence: The Vietnamese reader expects the onward links to stay inside the handbook and is not told that additional tests are documented in the packages' own external documentation.

findings.heading: ### Summary statistics (rstatix)
findings.proposition: English says get_summary_stats() can be used WITH grouped data ('It can be used with grouped data as well'); the translation says 'No cung co the duoc su dung de nhom so lieu' (it can also be used TO GROUP the data), attributing the grouping to get_summary_stats() rather than to the group_by() call shown in the chunk immediately below.
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader may expect get_summary_stats() itself to perform the grouping and omit the required group_by(hospital) step, getting ungrouped output.

findings.heading: ### T-test (rstatix)
findings.proposition: English instructs the reader to use a FORMULA syntax ('Use a formula syntax to specify the numeric and categorical columns'); the translation drops the word formula ('USu dung cu phap de chi dinh cot bien lien tuc va cot bien phan loai').
findings.reader_consequence: The Vietnamese reader is not told that age_years ~ gender is R formula notation, so the reusable concept behind the ~ operator is not named at the point it is introduced for rstatix.
